why: Isolation has a read half as well as a write half, and `storage-developer-writes-land-on-production-keys` only pins the write. Under this mutation a developer session WRITES to `tanks.dev.*` but READS the player's real keys, so it adopts the production campaign, the production legacy touch settings, and exports production data through save.ts -- while every write-side assertion still passes. `String(key)` rather than `key` so the mutation keeps the argument coercion the adapter does and differs only in the namespace mapping.
killedBy: a developer session cannot reach production data exports and imports through save.ts inside its own namespace
a developer session cannot reach production data neither adopts nor deletes the production legacy touch settings
createNamespacedStorage: developer cannot see a production key, however it was written
createNamespacedStorage: developer reads back its own writes
createNamespacedStorage: developer removes only its own key
the developer namespace over the whole store inventory persists across a reload: a second store bundle reads the first one back
